DCBO should remain in the LMS operating-layer universe as a US-listed AI-first LMS/product leader, but its primary exposure appears more enterprise-learning than university-specific and needs vertical verification.

NNI is a second-order campus infrastructure candidate: payments, tuition management, and education technology services may become integration points as LMS and student operating platforms consolidate workflows.

Several obvious LMS leaders are private or non-US primary-listed, including Instructure/Canvas, Anthology/Blackboard, and D2L; US-listed exposure may therefore appear through direct customers, adjacent SaaS platforms, payments, analytics, tutoring, and content tools rather than pure-play LMS vendors.

BNED should be tracked as a speculative LMS-adjacent course-materials and digital-access channel rather than a simple campus bookstore; verify digital courseware, publisher concentration, LMS integration, and liquidity risk.

NNI may be an underfollowed institutional infrastructure candidate if its Education Technology Services and Payments products integrate with LMS, SIS, student accounts, or campus payment workflows.

Need a dedicated evidence pass on US-listed AI tutoring, proctoring, accessibility, analytics, content-authoring, and assessment vendors to separate true LMS plug-ins from companies likely to be displaced by LMS-native bundles.
DCBO is the cleanest US-listed small-cap LMS / learning-platform proxy for the LMS operating-layer node; verify education vertical mix before elevating beyond Layer 1B.
APEI/Rasmussen is a high-quality customer-side signal: the migration from Blackboard to D2L included AI tutoring, feedback, content creation, and analytics, supporting the LMS-bundling hypothesis.

CHGG should be tracked as a speculative shadow candidate: it may be impaired by LMS-native AI tutoring/feedback, but content/skilling assets could become supplier or acquisition-relevant if validated by partnerships.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed vendors in accessibility, assessment, proctoring, plagiarism detection, student-success analytics, SIS integration, and content-authoring tools that may sit one layer downstream from LMS consolidation.

APEI should be tracked as a customer/operator signal for LMS-as-operating-layer adoption because Rasmussen and APUS provide concrete evidence of Brightspace plus AI tutoring, feedback, content creation, and analytics adoption.

BNED is a potential second-order course-materials and digital-access chokepoint adjacent to LMS workflows, but the thesis depends on verifying LMS integration, inclusive-access economics, and publisher/platform bargaining power.

NNI is an underfollowed adjacent infrastructure candidate through education technology services and payments rather than direct LMS software; later layers should verify whether ETSP integrates with LMS/SIS ecosystems.

The key node signal is not only LMS replacement but bundling: Brightspace, Lumi Tutor/Feedback, Creator+, and Performance+ suggest LMS vendors are absorbing tutoring, feedback, content creation, and analytics budgets.

Need a separate pass for non-US or private reference leaders, including D2L, Instructure, Anthology/Blackboard, PowerSchool, and private AI tutoring/assessment plug-ins, because they define the competitive map but do not meet the US-listed candidate constraint.

node: Learning-management systems expanding into institutional operating platforms
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe around the hypothesis that LMS platforms are becoming institutional operating layers through AI tutoring, feedback, analytics, content creation, payments, and workflow integrations. The strongest direct evidence is Rasmussen University, owned by American Public Education, selecting D2L Brightspace plus D2L Lumi, Creator+, Performance+, Lumi Tutor, and Lumi Feedback. Because several category leaders are private or non-US primary-listed, this pass emphasizes US-listed direct customers and adjacent platforms rather than only headline LMS vendors. Layer 1B expansion for the LMS-as-operating-layer node found that the more investable underfollowed lane is likely not the headline LMS vendor itself, because several category leaders are private or non-US listed, but adjacent public suppliers exposed to courseware access, curriculum/testing spend, AI tutoring, student support, analytics, payments, and institutional workflow infrastructure. The strongest underfollowed candidates for later verification are BNED as a campus-course-materials and digital access-code channel exposed to LMS/courseware bundling, APEI as a public customer/adoption signal for D2L-style LMS consolidation, NNI as an education technology/payments and systems infrastructure provider, and NRDY as a speculative AI tutoring/academic-support point solution that could either be embedded into LMS workflows or displaced by LMS-native AI bundles.
